title: Restore the verified Pico SDK environment in Release
goal: Replace the erroneous empty Release Pico bridge environment with the already verified vendor SDK environment used by the pre-Release collection workflow, without starting hardware.
doneWhen: Release launcher resolves its Pico Python interpreter to the existing verified vendor SDK environment.
The selected interpreter imports xrobotoolkit_sdk and the Release Pico bridge module.
Release documentation describes the verified external SDK environment accurately and does not claim that a new generic uv environment contains the vendor SDK.
No hardware, PC Service, Pico publisher, Ray cluster, camera, gripper, or robot session is started.
decisions: The previous task's separate pico_bridge/.venv was an incorrect environment boundary because it lacked the existing verified vendor SDK.
Release will reuse the verified Pico SDK environment until the vendor SDK has a reproducible, licensed installation artifact that can be managed directly by Release.

verification.summary: Release now defaults to the pre-Release verified XRoboToolkit SDK environment and imported the Release Pico bridge successfully without starting hardware.
checks: Verified existing XRoboToolkit environment imports xrobotoolkit_sdk, zmq, numpy, and yaml
Verified vendor SDK interpreter imports the Release vr_data_publisher module
Launcher shell syntax and verified SDK default path checks passed
No publisher, PC Service, Ray cluster, camera, gripper, or robot process was started
limitations: The vendor SDK environment remains external at ../pico_software/XRoboToolkit-Teleop-Sample-Python/.venv; use RLINF_PICO_SDK_VENV to select a verified compatible replacement on another host.
No hardware or end-to-end collection run was exercised.
